known.title: Load cold-read limits from the reviewed checkout
Gate: test_3's invalid-setting case expects the wrong command contract

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - a settings fix lands while an existing story worktree retains its previous forge.toml.
This reads the checkout running `forge next`, whereas `forge read SHOP` loads SHOP's own checkout and configuration (`src/forge/story.py:166-169`). If main sets the limit to 1 while SHOP still uses 2, next announces a stop after round 1 and offers `--resolve more`, but read rejects that resolution because SHOP has not reached its limit. The reverse mismatch hides a required owner choice. Both `_next_round` callers pass the reporting checkout, and the spec loop at nextstep.py:350 has the same fault. Load the configuration belonging to each reviewed story/spec.
findings.title: Load cold-read limits from the reviewed checkout

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - running the new test matrix's invalid case.
This invokes `forge next` and expects exit 1 with the exact validation refusal on stderr. However, next deliberately catches ordinary bad-config refusals (`src/forge/nextstep.py:146-151`), reports their first line through `_report_config` (`:470-475`), and returns 0 (`:183`). This freshly initialized fixture has no cold-read notes that would reach the newly added uncaught configuration reads. Consequently, the first invalid-value assertion fails even though validation works, preventing the required proof test from passing. Exercise validation through a command that propagates the refusal.
